title: SLO-driven quarantine lattice and deterministic fallthrough router for dependency/model/tenant failures
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Implement a deterministic decision lattice that synthesizes SLO signals (latency, error-rate, error-budget burn), regional health, and tenant priority to place a dependency/model/tenant into a ‘quarantine’ tier and route requests to safe fallthroughs. This ticket covers design, simulation, implementation hooks, and a staged rollout plan.

Motivation: Current per-entity trip logic is brittle: thresholds are static, noisy, and often cause noisy rollbacks. We need an SLO-aligned, multi-signal algorithm that: 
- reduces false-positive trips during transient spikes,
- guarantees deterministic fallback routing (no blackholes),
- provides graceful capacity shedding for overloaded GPUs while preserving high-priority tenants, and
- integrates with the Console for observability and on-call remediation.

Deliverables: 
1) Decision lattice algorithm and config schema (rate/error/latency/eburn/time-windows + hysteresis)
2) Simulation harness run against 3 canonical workloads (chat low-latency p50 workload, batch long-context throughput, bursty embedding spikes)
3) Runtime gating hooks: evaluation callback, trip marker, and failover routing table entries
4) Console dashboard + alerting playbook + incident runbook updates
5) Gradual rollout plan with canary cohorts and automated rollback triggers

Non-goals: global model-serving replumbing, fine-grained per-layer kernel selection (handled in separate perf tickets).
comments: 2026-03-10 Aisha Patel: Initial write-up and proposal attached. Linked design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/rpm/decision-lattice-draft (internal). Added simulation checklist and datasets.

2026-03-11 Miguel Ortega: Did an initial sanity-check of thresholds. Proposed using a two-window approach: short-window (30s) for spike detection and long-window (10m) for sustained e-burn. Set tentative thresholds: p99 latency > 1.6x baseline OR 30s error-rate > 5% AND 10m error-budget burn > 10% => quarantine candidate. Need simulation to validate.
2026-03-11 Priya Sharma (SRE): Reviewed and requested multi-region health incorporation (if primary region degraded, prefer region-fallback rather than model fallback). Added label 'multi-region'.

2026-03-12 Design review (Luca Chen): UX constraint: Console must show deterministic fallthrough path and the reason code for the quarantine (latency|errors|eburn|region). Add a ’manual override’ action for SREs with audit log.

2026-03-12 Miguel Ortega: Implemented simulation harness (repo: github.com/redwood-inference/safety-sim, PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/safety-sim/pull/14). Early results: short-window-only thresholds produce 32% false trips on bursty embedding workload. Two-window hysteresis reduces false trips to 7% while maintaining 94% success for high-priority tenants.

2026-03-13 Aisha Patel: Added rollout proposal: Canary cohort contains 2% of traffic (low QPS tenants), followed by 10% regional weight increase over 48h if SLO regressions < 0.5% and no P1 alerts. Automated rollback triggers: sustained 5% SLO drop or >3 P0 errors in 15m. Added monitoring queries and example dashboard panels.
2026-03-13 Security note (Ravi Kapoor): KMS access required for storing per-tenant escalation tokens for manual overrides. Marked security_review_required=true.
acceptance_criteria: Deterministic decision lattice implemented in runtime with feature flag gating
Simulation results showing <10% false-positive trips on canonical workloads
Console shows quarantine events with reason codes and fallthrough path; manual override with audit log exists
Canary rollout executed with automated rollback and metrics checks in place
Security review completed for override token handling and RBAC enforcement
work_items: Design: finalize lattice config schema and reason codes
Sim: run 3 canonical workload scenarios and produce false-trip / success matrices
Runtime: add trip evaluation hook, marker propagation in tracing, and routing table entries
Console: dashboard panels, per-event drilldown, and manual override UX
SRE: add alerts, playbook, and on-call runbook updates
Security: KMS/HSM integration for override tokens and audit logging
notes: Trade-offs discussed: conservative long-window thresholds reduce false trips but increase time-to-recovery for genuine regressions. Proposed mitigation: a 'fast-path' override for confirmed P0 incidents and automated diagnostics snapshotting to accelerate postmortems. Also considered probabilistic shedding (percent-based) but prefer deterministic lattice for predictable routing and auditability.
